headline: Back to profit as demand and cost discipline improve
summary_short: ManpowerGroup's Q2 2026 revenue rose 7.5% y/y (+7.8% q/q) to $4,860M, and the company swung to net earnings of $53.5M ($1.13 diluted EPS) from a $67.1M net loss a year earlier; adjusted diluted EPS (ex one-offs) was $0.99, +27% in constant currency.
summary_long: Revenue grew 7.5% y/y (5.8% constant currency) to $4,860M on strong Manpower-brand demand in the U.S., Latin America, APME, and select European markets. Gross profit rose only 2.2% y/y as cost of services grew faster (+8.6%), but SG&A fell 15.3% y/y — the prior year included an $88.7M Switzerland/U.K. impairment that did not recur — lifting operating profit to $112.0M from a $25.3M loss. Net earnings were $53.5M ($1.13 diluted EPS) versus a $67.1M loss a year earlier; the quarter included a $100M Jefferson Wells sale ($88M net proceeds) and one-off charges adding $0.14 to EPS. Cash fell to $180.6M on $585.8M of debt repayment. Q3 2026 diluted EPS is guided to $0.96–$1.06.

drivers.explanation: CEO Prising cited strong execution across brands and markets, continued cost discipline, and improving demand; Manpower brand grew very strongly with improving trends across Experis and Talent Solutions.

Strong demand in the U.S., Latin America, APME, and select European countries (Italy, Spain, Poland, Norway); Manpower brand very strong, Experis improved on U.S. strength, Talent Solutions gained on RPO with solid MSP growth.
Gross profit grew only 2.2% y/y versus 7.5% revenue growth because cost of services rose faster (+8.6% y/y), compressing gross margin; the release does not itemize the mix/pricing cause.

Gross profit growth combined with an SG&A reduction; SG&A fell 15.3% y/y partly because the prior-year quarter included an $88.7M goodwill/intangible impairment in Switzerland and the U.K. that did not recur.

The Jefferson Wells sale, transformation costs, restructuring costs, and a discontinued-business liquidation charge together added $0.14 to EPS; excluding these, adjusted diluted EPS was $0.99, +27% in constant currency.

Six-month financing activities used $636.8M of cash, primarily $585.8M of long-term debt repayment, pulling cash down from $871.0M at 2025 year-end; the specific quarterly driver is not broken out separately.
